raw_response:
I farm these 18 mu the same way I have for many years, wheat first and then maize right after. I only have 2 people at home and some work is off-farm, so I cannot make the plan too complicated. For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too much because if wheat turns weak in spring, the yield loss is hard to recover. But I also cannot spend freely, so I will use a solid base fertilizer, then one main topdress and only add more if the stand looks yellow. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate at the key stages, not too many times. For maize, the time after wheat harvest is very tight, so I will keep the usual summer maize and hire machine work if needed to get it planted fast. I watch what nearby farmers do, and around here if maize goes in late, yield drops quickly, so speed matters more than fancy management. I use practical rates, a little on the safe side, because under-applying usually worries me more than wasting a little fertilizer.
